newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * The Romanian government is expected to decide on increasing the health budget to 3.2 percent of gross domestic product, up from a previous 2.8 during its weekly session.

* The U.S. Senate has passed a Republican initiative to ask U.S. President Bill Clintom to invite Romania's President Emil Constantinescu for an official trip to Washinghton, Romania's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Gilda Lazar said.

* Ukraine and Romania need the bilateral treaty to set the bases of cooperation between the two neighbours, said Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin before meeting Ukraine's deputy foreign minister Anton Buteiko.

* Greece supports Romania's bid to join NATO and the European Union, said visiting Greek Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos during his talks with President Emil Constantinescu and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.

* Marin Condescu, leader of the miners' trade union confederation, asked President Emil Constantinescu to help the creation of a joint commission -- unions, employers and government -- to watch the restructuring of mining.
* Agrostar union federation, representing employees in state-owned farms, protested in Bucharest against the government's farming policy.
